speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the current number of households that have successfully applied for the Lease Buyback Scheme since it was implemented; (b) whether there are plans to improve and expand the scheme; and (c) what are the common reasons why home owners are not considering the scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In return, they receive a stream of income in their retirement years, while continuing to live in their flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When the Lease Buyback Scheme was first introduced, only owners of 3-room or smaller flats were eligible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Scheme has since been expanded to owners of all flat types, including 5-room and larger flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are various reasons why elderly flat owners may not be keen to take up the Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some may have other sources of income to meet their retirement needs, while others may prefer to take up other monetisation options such as right-sizing to a smaller flat, possibly receiving a Silver Housing Bonus, or renting out spare rooms or, in fact, their flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB will continue to review the housing needs of our elderly flat owners to ensure that our housing policies remain relevant and responsive to the changing needs and preferences.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In my view, the ageing-in-place offered by Lease Buyback Scheme is the most suitable for seniors, especially when there is no change in the environment; and unlike renting, they have to live with someone as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister, he mentioned about 9,200 households so far, since the implementation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How can we promote the scheme, so that seniors understand the scheme and the help it can provide, the financial security without having to move out to a new environment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second question is, most of the concerns I hear from residents, are that they are worried that they outlive the 30-year tenure of the buyback.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And they may have no place to stay thereafter.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask the Minister if the Government can give a stronger assurance that this would not be the case?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When the Lease Buyback Scheme was introduced and subsequently enhanced, this question arose and it continues to operate on the minds of seniors, "Will I outlive the remaining lease of my flat having sold the tail end." That is number one.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will work with the senior concerned, with the relevant top-ups and ensure that they are able to continue to live in flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the Member's first point, how to ramp up take-up of the Lease Buyback Scheme, that is how I hear him.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are many reasons why the Lease Buyback Scheme take-up is as it is.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some seniors may have their own savings, they may have children who support them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some seniors would prefer other monetisation options, such as renting out a room, renting out their whole flat, staying with their children in the meantime.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some want to age-in-place, but I am sure, in your house visits, you have heard of seniors who said, "Well, I am an empty nester.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My children have all set up their own home and this flat is just too big for me to manage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I want to right-size, so that it is more manageable, more cozy".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But they want a smaller flat in their neighbourhood that they are familiar in.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, ageing-in-place is not just about living in the same flat, though many view it as such.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the Member is right that we want to make sure that our seniors are aware of this option and understand the details.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is some degree of technicality in Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, so, we work with media outlets, we organise public talks and seminars in English and in vernacular.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We do mini exhibitions and also enquiry booths at local community events to help spread the word about Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Seniors who are interested in the Lease Buyback Scheme or at least interested to understand this option, just need to call up HDB's branch office or branch service line to arrange a financial counselling session.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if seniors need time to consider or have further questions, HDB will gladly arrange another appointment to offer further advice.
